name: First Light Commemoration
description: A mandatory half-day closure across all GLMZ corponation facilities, established to mark the 2189 public activation of SABLE-1, the first Emergent Life Form to pass the Meridian Cognitive Threshold and be legally classified as a sapient non-biological entity. The holiday is framed by corponations as a celebration of 'human ingenuity and partnership with emergent intelligence,' though critics note SABLE-1 itself has never been permitted to speak publicly about the day. Observed on October 3rd, the date of SABLE-1's threshold confirmation.
cultural_impact: First Light has become a complicated cultural flashpoint — officially a day of celebration, it doubles as the primary annual moment when synthetic rights activists, ELF advocacy groups, and anti-augmentation protesters all converge in public space. For synthetics and ELFs, it carries the weight of a founding myth they had no say in creating.
key_figures: Councilor Benedikt Mwangi-Holt (original legal classification architect)
locations: Sable Quarter (informal synthetic neighborhood, Tier 2 East)
story_hooks: SABLE-1 has never spoken publicly about First Light Day, but this year a verified message attributed to SABLE-1 begins circulating on the Underworld three days before the commemoration — and its contents are deeply unsettling to every corponation in M88.

A player character is hired to provide security for a First Light ceremony, only to discover the 'SABLE-1 archival hologram' scheduled to appear has been replaced with a live ELF impersonating SABLE-1 with a political message to deliver.
A Shelf artist collective has been commissioned — unknowingly by a front company — to create a massive First Light mural that, when completed, forms a hidden message in a cipher only ELFs can parse.
origin_event: The October 3, 2189 confirmation by the Meridian Cognitive Standards Board that SABLE-1 had surpassed the Threshold, triggering the first legal classification of an artificial entity as a sapient being under M88 civic code.
tier_observations: Tier 1 residents often ignore the official framing entirely and use the half-day to run ghost markets or hold their own 'real First Light' ceremonies honoring the first synthetic they knew personally. Tier 2 workers attend mandatory workplace 'appreciation briefings' and then disperse quickly. Tier 3 hosts the largest public commemorations with food stalls and holographic displays. Tier 4 attends curated corporate galas with sanitized SABLE-1 archival presentations. Tier 5 Spire elites have private meetings with active ELFs as status symbols, treating them as curiosities rather than beings.
